definitions.definition: Process of checking that a logic design meets its specification by asking whether the proposed design does what is intended.
Technique that runs a software model of a design while a testbench supplies inputs, observes outputs and checks them.
Technique imitating a design under development on special-purpose hardware, usually compiled from an HDL, mainly for debugging and functional verification.
Technique mapping a design onto reconfigurable hardware that runs much faster than software simulation and allows testing with real software, though large designs take long to implement.
Use of mathematical methods to prove or disprove that a design satisfies stated properties without test vectors, limited by state-space explosion.
Formal technique performing a systematic, exhaustive exploration of a mathematical model of a system; often automatic, but generally unable to scale to large systems.
Approach in which the tester has no knowledge of the internal structure of the item under test.
Approach giving the tester extensive visibility into the internals of the item under test.
Approach in which the tester has only partial knowledge of internal structure, combining the visibility-free and full-visibility styles to find structural or usage defects.
Integrated circuit that combines most or all key components of a computer or electronic system onto a single microchip.
definitions.unitTitle: Overview of SoC Architectures and Functional Verification Environment

definitions.definition: Advantages over discrete multi-chip systems: lower power use, smaller die area, lower cost and higher reliability from fewer packages and reduced assembly.
definitions.unitTitle: Overview of SoC Architectures and Functional Verification Environment

definitions.definition: Alternative to a shared bus for linking the processor cores, memories and interfaces of a single-chip system.
definitions.unitTitle: Overview of SoC Architectures and Functional Verification Environment

definitions.definition: Simulation environment that generates stimuli, drives them into the design, monitors the outputs and checks the results.
definitions.unitTitle: Overview of SoC Architectures and Functional Verification Environment

definitions.definition: Testbench component that creates input vectors intended to expose differences between a specification and its implementation.
definitions.unitTitle: Overview of SoC Architectures and Functional Verification Environment

definitions.definition: Component that validates that stored transactions are legal and compares actual results against expected results supplied by the generator.
definitions.unitTitle: Overview of SoC Architectures and Functional Verification Environment

definitions.definition: Component that compares a design's inputs and outputs against an expected relationship, often defined by a predictor model, to judge conformance.
definitions.unitTitle: Overview of SoC Architectures and Functional Verification Environment

definitions.definition: Metric of how thoroughly the HDL source is exercised, for example by statement, branch and toggle measures.
definitions.unitTitle: Overview of SoC Architectures and Functional Verification Environment

definitions.definition: Metric showing whether the intended functionality described in the verification plan has actually been exercised.
definitions.unitTitle: Overview of SoC Architectures and Functional Verification Environment

definitions.definition: Reaching the predefined coverage goals, signalling that verification of the planned features is complete.
definitions.unitTitle: Overview of SoC Architectures and Functional Verification Environment

definitions.definition: IEEE 1800 hardware description and verification language that extends Verilog, originating from Superlog donated to Accellera in 2002.
Programming language for verifying designs written in an HDL, combining high-level programming features with bit-level manipulation.
Array whose size is set at run time rather than fixed at compile time.
Array indexed by a key of a user-specified type instead of a contiguous integer range.
Variable-size ordered collection that supports efficient insertion and removal at both ends.
Construct that bundles related signals together, reducing repetitive port declarations between modules.
Declaration inside a signal bundle that specifies signal direction for each module or testbench using it.
Named group of signals sharing one clock, each sampled or driven at set times relative to the clock edge to avoid races with the design.
Testbench container holding tasks, functions, class objects and initial blocks, executed in the reactive region so testbench code sees settled design values.
Parallel construct in which the parent thread waits until every spawned thread has finished.
Parallel construct in which the parent resumes once any one spawned thread finishes while the others keep running.
Parallel construct in which the parent continues immediately after spawning its threads without waiting.
Copy that creates a new object and copies field values field by field, so reference fields still point at the same underlying objects as the original.
Copy that also duplicates the objects referenced by fields, so the copy and original share no contents and later changes to one do not affect the other.
Property declared so that a single copy is shared by all instances of its class; a static method can be called without creating an object.
Named class member in curly braces whose active instances are solved together as one logical AND, with no priority or source order.
Stimulus technique that declares variables as randomisable with constraints, then calls a built-in method to produce legal random values.
Built-in method that enables or disables individual constraints of an object at run time.
Construct controlling the sequence in which random variables are solved, instead of relying on source order, when one choice constrains another.
Class model in which each class derives from at most one parent class, as supported by SystemVerilog together with interface classes.
Provision of one interface to entities of different data types, letting code work with values of more than one type.
Form letting one name refer to objects of several classes sharing a common superclass, with the method to run usually resolved at run time.
Handle declared inside a class that points to an interface instance already present in a module, giving class-based components access to real design signals.
Static object handle used to synchronise concurrent processes: one process triggers it and others wait for it.
Container holding a fixed number of keys that processes take to proceed and return when done, used for mutual exclusion over shared resources.
Built-in FIFO channel for passing messages between processes, either bounded, which blocks writers when full, or unbounded.
Check executed like the condition of an if statement inside a procedural block, passing when true at execution time; intended for simulation only.
Check not tied to procedural execution that is evaluated over clock ticks and is required for formal verification.
Assertion building block describing a scenario that unfolds over time, built with temporal operators such as the cycle-delay operator.
Assertion building block specifying required behaviour, often a triggering sequence implying that further behaviour must follow.
Reusable type bundling coverpoints, cross coverage, a sampling event and options, instantiated with new like a class.
Coverage item that tracks one variable or expression and records which of its legal values occur during a test.
Coverage that tracks combinations of values across two or more coverpoints rather than each one alone.
Standard mechanism that lets SystemVerilog call C or C++ functions and lets foreign code call SystemVerilog functions.
Plain class describing one unit of interface activity, with randomisable fields for the driver and fields the monitor fills in.
Component that takes transactions from a mailbox and drives them onto the design's ports through a virtual interface.
Component that watches the interface without driving it, rebuilds transactions from observed signals and forwards them to the scoreboard.
Container class with no logic of its own that creates the driver, monitor and scoreboard, connects their handles and starts them.
Top-level code that creates the environment and supplies stimulus, such as a write followed by a read-back of the same address.
Model defining the expected input-output relationship of the design, against which the scoreboard judges whether the design meets its specification.
Non-synthesizable software model of a component with external buses, simulating bus transactions so bus behaviour can be checked before hardware exists.
Accellera-standard, class-based methodology adding a framework and automation to SystemVerilog for verifying integrated circuit designs.
Wrapper class grouping the verification objects for one design interface, containing a driver and monitor when active or only a monitor when passive.
Component handling scenario generation for the design, including initial-state setup and configuration of the environment.
